news.title: Purdue MEM students teamed up with Kaaro Health to strengthen rural healthcare operations in Uganda
news.summary_en: A team of Purdue University Master of Engineering Management (MEM) students partnered with Kaaro Health, a social enterprise that provides affordable healthcare to underserved rural communities in Uganda, to develop technology and operations solutions that support the organization’s continued growth.

news.title: PaveX, founded by CCE's Jahanshahi, receives NSF funding to help agencies plan road repairs sooner
news.summary_en: PaveX, a Purdue University-related startup that uses advanced AI to automate road condition assessments and help public works departments maintain infrastructure, has received a $305,000 Phase I Small Business Innovation Research grant from the National Science Foundation (NSF) to develop its technology.

news.title: Indianapolis profile: Lindsey Laine
news.summary_en: Lindsey Laine has taken advantage of close connection opportunities in Indianapolis with leaders from some of the largest companies in the medical and healthcare industries.

news.title: Purdue Biofuels Consortium to bring biodiesel and ethanol blends to diesel engines
news.summary_en: Could tractors start using ethanol as fuel? That’s the project being tackled by Purdue University, John Deere, Cummins, and a consortium of biofuel producers.

news.title: Cars, engineering and Ironman competitions fuel first-year student's success
news.summary_en: A passion for cars and engineering, combined with a determination to challenge himself, led Alec Staley to Purdue University.

news.title: Purdue Engineering's Blue Sky competition winners aim to monitor early disease biomarkers and scale quantum computing
news.summary_en: "Blue sky" is a well-known expression for thinking out of the box. It's apt naming for a Purdue Engineering initiative that supports high-risk, high-reward research ideas with the potential to address major societal challenges before they become mainstream research priorities.
